title: Where does the middle of a sliding ladder go?
desc:
Where does the middle of a sliding ladder go? Guess first: A, B or C.

Lean a ladder against a wall and let it slide down. Its middle traces a perfect quarter-circle centred on the corner: the midpoint of a right triangle's longest side is always the same distance from all three corners, so it stays exactly half a ladder from the corner the whole way down. Every other point on the ladder traces an ellipse (the same idea as the trammel of Archimedes, a tool for drawing ellipses). And all the positions of the ladder together wrap a star-shaped curve called the astroid.

TRY IT ON PAPER: draw a right angle. Take a strip of card 10 cm long, mark its middle, and slide its two ends along the two lines, dotting the middle as you go. Then try a point 3 cm from one end.

YOUR TURN: why is the middle always half a ladder from the corner? Answer in the comments.
